title: platform-standup-2026-04-02
content:
Platform Engineering — Standup notes — 2026-04-02

Attendees: Ava Martinez (owner), Lina Chen, Marcus Reed, Diego Alvarez, remote: Priya Nair

Quick status updates
- Ava: Control plane rollout testing for multi-tenant isolation finished smoke tests yesterday. Found 2 edge cases around tenant-scoped cache invalidation (see PLAT-2145). Rolling a hotfix branch.
- Lina: Routing policy work — canary routing now supports cost-tier aware routing. Deployed to staging; need perf metrics but functional tests passed.
- Marcus: Auth & quotas — rate-limiter prototype integrated with KMS auth token flow. Observed token lookup latency spikes under burst; investigating Redis connection pool config.
- Diego: Observability & tracing — added per-route token-level tracing tags; sending example traces to dev ops stack. Working on dashboard panels for quota throttling.
- Priya (ops, remote): Validating Dedicated pool fallback behavior across regions; noted inconsistent fallback to compatible model variant in eu-west-1 during simulated outage.

Blockers / Risks
- Cache invalidation bug (Ava) — tenant cache keys sometimes colliding for short-lived sessions. Impact: stale KV cache can return wrong prefix when using shared caches for model variants. Temporary mitigation: tighten key namespace; full fix requires change to cache sharding (PLAT-2145). Owner: Ava + Lina. ETA: patch by EOD tomorrow.
- Redis connection spikes (Marcus) — under synthetic burst tests, connection saturation leads to auth token delays -> client timeouts. Short-term: increase pool, add connection backoff. Longer-term: move to multiplexed connection / sidecar caching. Owner: Marcus. Dep: infra team.
- Canary routing metric gaps (Lina) — we’re not capturing cost-per-token for some model variants due to missing tags on older model artifacts. Need small instrumentation PR. Owner: Lina. JIRA: PLAT-2190.

Notes by area
1) Control plane (Ava)
- Hotfix branch for cache key namespace created: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/842. Running staging smoke.
- Planning a localized canary to validate cache invalidation fix across 3 tenants before global rollout.
- Action: schedule 30m post-mortem with infra and serving-runtime if hotfix uncovers deeper kv layout issues.

2) Routing (Lina)
- Canary routing for cost-tier aware routing is in staging. Need to validate latency SLO against dedicated policy (target p95 < 120ms token time).
- Observed routing fallthrough for model alias mapping when fallback rules chain > 2. Lina to add unit tests and integration test scenario.
- Action: Lina to add cost tagging to older model artifacts (PLAT-2190).

3) Auth & Quotas (Marcus)
- Integrated rate limiter with KMS-auth tokens. Quota counters stored in Redis; spikes cause token verification latency.
- Interim change: bump Redis client pool to 50 and enable client-side batching of quota increments. Marcus to deploy to staging and monitor for 24h.
- Discussion: move to a local in-process token cache for short-lived requests to avoid round-trip to Redis for each call. Tradeoff: slight staleness vs latency improvement. Follow-up spike test planned.

4) Observability & Dashboards (Diego)
- Added quota-throttle dashboard panels to console. Need UX review before wider rollout.
- Traces: added token-level tags, enabling correlate requests->quota decisions. Diego will demo in next ops sync.

Action items & owners
- Ava + Lina: finalize cache sharding fix, PR review and staging validation. Due: 2026-04-03 EOD.
- Marcus: deploy Redis pool/batching changes to staging and run 4h burst test. Due: 2026-04-02 EOD.
- Lina: create instrumentation PR for cost-per-token tagging (PLAT-2190). Due: 2026-04-05.
- Diego: UX review request for quota dashboards + demo in next ops meeting. Due: 2026-04-06.
- Priya: reproduce dedicated pool fallback issue in eu-west-1 and capture logs/trace ids. Due: 2026-04-04.

Notes to self / informal
- "Notes to self": check whether cache key collisions are correlated with certain model versioning patterns (e.g., alias reuse during rollout).
- Lingering question: should per-tenant cache be default for Dedicated customers? Pros: isolation. Cons: memory/cost. Add to roadmap discussion.

Meeting decisions
- Proceed with hotfix -> localized canary -> global rollout if staging stable for 24h.
- Move forward with temporary Redis client pool increase; parallel design work for multiplexed solution.

Linked references
- Control plane design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLAT/Control+Plane+Design
- Jira tickets: PLAT-2145 (cache collision), PLAT-2190 (cost tagging), PLAT-2210 (redis pool tuning)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/842

Next standup: 2026-04-03 09:30 PT

End of notes
